clue.text: Diplomat made to stick to the point

indicators.note: to here means added onto the end, so the point follows

parts.note: to fasten or fix one thing to another is to make it stick
E, east, is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: An envoy is told to keep strictly to the matter under discussion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the point' reads as one idiom, but the point is a compass point, E.
explanation.definitionFit: An attaché is a junior official on an embassy's diplomatic staff.

clue.text: High spot of getting married in a church

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in tells us the married abbreviation sits inside the other letters

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The best moment of a wedding is the church ceremony itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An acme is a peak or highest point, literally or figuratively.

parts.note: taken as written
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: Someone takes a journey into town.
explanation.definitionFit: A tour is a journey or excursion, a synonym for a trip.

indicators.note: freely suggests the letters move about without constraint into a new order

explanation.surface: An open-minded person lets oil be caught however it falls.
explanation.walkthrough: Catholic in its older sense means wide-ranging or broad-minded, not the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Catholic can mean universal or broad in sympathies, which is a liberal outlook.

clue.text: Examining some money in great detail

indicators.note: some, with detail, says only a part of these words' letters is wanted
this word says the answer sits inside the words it governs, as a run of their own consecutive letters

explanation.surface: Someone scrutinises a sum of cash very closely.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits in mon(EY IN G)reat; 'some ... detail' points to the letters drawn out of these words.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeing something, here spelt without the middle E, is looking at it closely.

definitions.meaning: a source of water rising from the ground, like a well
the season that comes ahead of summer in the year

explanation.definitionFit: Spring is both a natural water source and the season preceding summer.

clue.text: Animals seem unhappy coming up onto the vessel

indicators.note: onto, in a down clue, puts the next piece beneath the vessel

parts.note: a pan is a cooking vessel

indicators.note: in a down entry, coming up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: unhappy means sad

explanation.surface: Creatures look miserable as they are brought up on board a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Pandas are bears of China, so they are animals by example.

parts.note: de-creasing read literally is taking creases out, as with an iron; the phrase also means resolving problems

explanation.definitionFit: To iron something out is to smooth away creases or settle problems.

parts.note: a government's preliminary proposals for discussion, joked about as if its colour meant ecological concerns

explanation.walkthrough: A green paper is a UK government discussion document published before firm policy.
explanation.definitionFit: In the UK a green paper is a government consultation document, so green is not about ecology.

clue.text: Man out in storm reaching peak

indicators.note: storm, used as a verb, tells us these letters are thrown about violently

explanation.surface: A man caught outdoors in a tempest reaches the summit.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain has a peak, and peak stands for the whole mountain by extension.

definitions.meaning: split as come in, meaning to enter or move forward

explanation.definitionFit: Income is money earned, and split in two it reads as come in, to advance inwards.

indicators.note: badly signals these letters are put together wrongly, rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone named Jack has grown old in a poor way.
explanation.walkthrough: Jack, or jack tar, is an old name for a sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea dog is an old sailor, and jack is slang for a sailor.

parts.note: reads like the title of a London livery guild, but means a gathering of people at worship

explanation.definitionFit: The assembled people at a church service are its gathered worshippers.

parts.note: suggests an accountant analysing numbers, but means someone who smashes religious images

explanation.definitionFit: An iconoclast originally destroyed religious statues and images; the figures are statues.

clue.text: Running nose to nose and ready

indicators.note: running suggests the letters run about into a new order

explanation.surface: Two runners neck and neck are poised for the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on your toes is an idiom for being alert and prepared.

indicators.note: possibly says these letters may be arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A quoted spread of heat readings is being described.
explanation.definitionFit: Centigrade describes the Celsius scale used to measure temperature.

definitions.note: the 's stands for is, joining definition and wordplay

indicators.note: in the sound says we hear the word rather than read it

parts.note: roads, or a roadstead, is a sheltered anchorage for ships

explanation.surface: A Greek island's harbour lies in a stretch of water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound' looks like a strait of sea water, fitting the harbour picture, but it signals a homophone.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Aegean, near Turkey.

clue.text: Proceed to a port in India

parts.note: proceed means go
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone sets off for an Indian harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Goa is a coastal state and former Portuguese trading port on India's west coast.

clue.text: Gossip from spiteful female about jerk

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: a cat is slang for a malicious woman
a hitch is a sudden pull or jerk

explanation.surface: Tittle-tattle spread by a nasty woman about some idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' looks like an insult for a man; here it is a sudden tug.
explanation.definitionFit: Chit-chat is light idle talk, close to gossip.

definitions.meaning: a woman under a vow of celibacy never weds
the title used for a woman in a religious order

explanation.definitionFit: Nuns are called Sister and take a vow of chastity, so never marry.

definitions.meaning: a rowdy fight or disorderly fracas

explanation.definitionFit: A roughhouse is a violent disturbance; split, it reads as a crude dwelling.

clue.text: When one chooses a woven fabric

parts.note: taken as written
twill is a fabric woven with diagonal ribs

explanation.surface: Picking a cloth at one's own discretion.
explanation.definitionFit: At will means whenever or however one wishes.

clue.text: The other acts could be very expensive

indicators.note: could be says the letters might form something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: The remaining performers would charge a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: To cost the earth is an idiom for being extremely expensive.

indicators.note: contains means the article holds the next word within it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a lie is an untruth, an inaccuracy

explanation.surface: A piece from abroad turns out to have an error in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien means belonging to another country, which is foreign.

indicators.note: jump tells the letters to leap into a new order

explanation.surface: A fugitive skips bail by fleeing to an island in Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jump bail' reads as one idiom for absconding; 'Jump' alone is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Bali is an Indonesian island in South-East Asia.

definitions.meaning: a slimy creature that eats plants
a bullet or small piece of metal

explanation.definitionFit: A slug is both a shell-less mollusc that damages plants and a bullet or pellet.

clue.text: Is preceded by a fellow dandy

indicators.note: preceded by means the following pieces come before the first word

parts.note: taken as written
a don is a college fellow at a university
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fop is defined by the man ahead of him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' comes first in the clue but last in the answer, because it is preceded by A and DON.
explanation.definitionFit: An Adonis is a very handsome young man, a vain beau or dandy by extension.

indicators.note: at joins the two pieces in order

parts.note: high is slang for intoxicated
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A nightclub doorman who is intoxicated at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: A bouncer in cricket is a ball that rears up high; the doorman picture misleads.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bouncer is a short ball pitched to rise high toward the batter.

clue.text: Struggle with various results when not right

indicators.note: various suggests the letters take a different arrangement
when not tells us a letter is excluded from the pool

explanation.surface: A hard fight produces mixed outcomes when things go wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: Take R from RESULTS ('when not right') and rearrange ESULTS, as 'various' signals.
explanation.definitionFit: A tussle is a vigorous struggle or scuffle.

definitions.meaning: love is zero in tennis scoring
a duck is a score of zero in cricket

explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean zero: love in tennis and a duck in cricket.
